experiments.title: Time to notice
experiments.researchQuestion: How does changing the speed of continuous movement alter the feeling of stillness versus tension?
experiments.conceptConnection: Comparing still elements with slow movement can help examine how unpredictable transitions relate to uncertainty.
steps: Open the built-in visual test. Keep its fixed settings unchanged.
Select each trial in order and watch for the same short period.
Write what visibly changes in each trial before adding an emotional interpretation.
experiments.observableEvidence: Record the visible arrangement, movement, or grouping. Note no visible difference if that is what you see.
experiments.technicalQuestion: How does movement speed affect what you can follow?
experiments.emotionalQuestion: Does the slow movement trial feel more like waiting or hesitation?
experiments.constraintCheck: Use slow motion at a comfortable brightness. Stop if the display causes discomfort.

experiments.title: How much is enough?
experiments.researchQuestion: How does varying the number of slowly moving marks shift the sense of visual crowding?
experiments.conceptConnection: Adjusting the mark count allows you to test whether sparse or crowded arrangements better capture anxious over-stimulation.
